about: The four sites the newsroom's pages are served from, and which top-level sections each one owns. A page belongs to the site that owns its first path segment; a section no site names belongs to the main site. 'home' is the address a link to the site's pages uses (its permanent name); 'serve_at' is where its repository is served today (the main site is staged at site.php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai, the address its DNS record names, until the cutover, when php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai moves to it). The data and the team's records are their own repositories; team here is the team's pages.

site.what: the main UI: the homes, the briefings, the questions, the stories, the tools, the risk graph, the views

refs.what: the references: a page per source and per fact, who said what, the graphs of what the sources say, Wikipedia, the code read from the fix, Pulse, the vaults

updates.what: the regular updates: the state of affairs and its versions, the desk, the loops, how each section changed, what is new, the feeds

team.what: the newsroom's own pages: the team, the schedule, the board, the briefs, the members' rounds, the Sherpa, the feedback, the pipeline's status
team.own_about: what the repository writes itself, besides README.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE, .gitignore, .github/, press.json and the two tools the press installs: the partition never touches them, and the site's gate allows nothing else

runtime.about: What every site keeps its own copy of: the version its pages check, the 404 router that answers view addresses (/agencies/as/security/) and .well-known/. Everything else a page loads comes from one place: assets/ from the press (/v/<version>/assets/), data/ from the data API (/v/<version>/), a page of another site's section from that site (the editor, 25 October 2026: one source for every file).

never.about: v1's sources: the build, its content, the security notes, the agents' tools and the repository's own documents. They stay in v1 (and move to their own repositories in pass two); no site serves them.

elsewhere.about: Never copied into a site: served once, and every page's links, its route (<meta name="p2s-route"> for assets/route.js) and its Content-Security-Policy name the host.
